City Boy Movement Set For Ogun Executive Inauguration, Empowerment Programme

City Boy Movement Set For Ogun Executive Inauguration, Empowerment Programme

October 29, 2026 · CBM OGUN

presence in the state.

The movement announced the development in a post on its official X handle on Saturday, October 3, saying the event would feature the inauguration of its Ogun State executive, an empowerment programme and the commissioning of its state secretariat.

“The City Boy Movement is set to storm Ogun State for the official inauguration of the Ogun State Executive,” the movement said.

According to the statement, the programme will be held under the leadership of the movement’s State Patron, Alh Kamorudeen Olawale Yusuf, and State Director, Dr Lateef Sulaimon.


The movement said the activities were part of efforts to strengthen its structures and increase its presence at the grassroots across Ogun State.

“The activities reflect the Movement’s continued expansion of its organisational structure and grassroots presence in Ogun state,” the statement added.

Personal Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Special Duties, Alhaji Kamorudeen Yusuf

He formally accepted the appointment, pledging commitment to the objectives of the movement and the re-election campaign of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“With deep humility and a strong sense of duty, I hereby accept this responsibility. As always, I remain fully committed to serving passionately, diligently, and loyally in furtherance of the strategic interests of our Leader and the successful re-election bid of our Principal, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR,” he stated.

Lateef also expressed appreciation to Yusuf for what he described as consistent leadership and confidence in his ability to lead the structure in the state.

“I wish to sincerely appreciate our Leader, Hon. Kamorudeen O. Yusuf, for the confidence reposed in me and for his steadfast leadership of this movement. His vision, consistency, and belief in the strength of our structure continue to inspire us all to greater service,” he said.
